abstracts.title: TNFα promotes brain-predominant EAE independent of IFNγ and IL-17A in HLA-DR3 transgenic mice.
abstracts.abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is thought to be mediated by human leukocyte antigen (HLA) class II-restricted autoreactive CD4 T cells producing interleukin (IL)-17A and/or interferon γ (IFNγ), but the necessity of these cytokines for disease pathogenesis is unclear. Utilizing HLA-DR3 (DRβ1*0301) transgenic mice lacking IFNγ or IL-17A in experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE), a model of MS, we found that neither cytokine is essential for disease induction, although both have distinct roles. The absence of IFNγ caused atypical, brain-predominant EAE characterized by high levels of IL-17A, while the absence of IL-17A resulted in classical EAE, targeting the spinal cord. To assess whether IL-17A drives atypical EAE in the absence of IFNγ, we generated HLA-DR3.IFNγ-/-.IL-17A-/- double knockout (DKO) mice. DKO mice developed atypical EAE with brain infiltration and inflammation of the brainstem and cerebellum, indicating that IL-17A is dispensable for brain-predominant disease in the absence of IFNγ. DKO mice exhibited significant CD4 T cell infiltration and increased expression of CD4 T cell-associated genes at peak disease. Prior to central nervous system infiltration, CD4 T cell…

abstracts.title: Th17 suppression strategies: targeting IL-17 and RORγt pathways in autoimmune diseases.
abstracts.abstract: T helper 17 (Th17) cells and their key effector cytokine, particularly IL-17A and IL-17F, play central roles in host defense against extracellular pathogens. However, they are also critically involved in the pathogenesis of many autoimmune and inflammatory diseases. Th17 cell differentiation, stabilization, plasticity, and pathogenicity are regulated by a network of cytokines and transcription factors, including IL-6, TGF-β, IL-23, STAT3, and the key transcription factor RORγt. RORγt-dependent pathways are also relevant to other immune populations, including group 3 innate lymphoid cells (ILC3s), highlighting the complexity of the IL-17 axis across tissues. Dysregulation of these pathways can lead to chronic inflammation and tissue damage in diseases such as psoriasis, rheumatoid arthritis, multiple sclerosis, and inflammatory bowel disease. Therapeutic targeting of the Th17 axis has led to clinically established approaches, particularly direct blockade of IL-17 signaling and inhibition of IL-23, whereas direct RORγt inhibition remains an investigational strategy. RORγt inhibitors may modulate Th17 differentiation and broader RORγt-dependent transcriptional programs, but their cli…

Study on the relationship between disease progression and changes in Th17/Treg levels in patients with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis.
abstracts.abstract: Objective This study aims to investigate the relationship between disease progression and changes in Th17/Treg levels in patients with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS). Methods This retrospective study analyzed clinical data and Th17/Treg cell levels from 130 RRMS patients and 100 non-inflammatory neurological disease controls treated between December 2021 and January 2025. Th17 cells were identified as CD4 + IL-17A + cells and Treg cells as CD4 + CD25 + Foxp3 + cells via flow cytometry. Results The two groups were comparable in baseline characteristics ( p > 0.05). The proportion of CD4 + IL-17A + Th17 cells was significantly higher in RRMS patients than in controls (4.26 ± 1.35% vs. 1.52 ± 0.47%, p + CD25 + Foxp3 + Treg cells were significantly lower (2.91 ± 0.98% vs. 5.38 ± 1.52%, p p p r = 0.521, p r = 0.485, p r = -0.387, p Conclusion Th17/Treg imbalance may be an important mechanism underlying RRMS pathogenesis and disease progression. Modulating this balance may represent a promising therapeutic target for RRMS.

abstracts.title: Repulsive guidance molecule-a regulates neutrophil-associated Th17 responses in CNS autoimmunity.
abstracts.abstract: Background and aim Repulsive guidance molecule-A (RGMa) is well-known for its roles in T-cell-mediated neuroinflammation and CNS repair. Innate-adaptive immune interactions, particularly between neutrophils and Th17 cells, are emerging as critical drivers of neuroinflammatory pathology in multiple sclerosis (MS). Whether RGMa regulates these neutrophil-associated Th17 responses remains largely unknown. Elucidating this mechanism may reveal novel therapeutic targets for MS. Methods Serum levels of RGMa, BMP4, neutrophil elastase (NE), IL-17A, and inflammatory markers were measured in 10 relapsing-remitting MS patients during acute relapse and remission phases, and in 10 healthy controls. In vitro transwell co-cultures using primary human neutrophils and CD3 + T cells were employed to evaluate the effects of RGMa monoclonal antibody (RGMa-mAb) treatment on neutrophil activation, Th17-associated responses, and T-cell migration. In parallel, experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) mice were treated with RGMa-mAb to assess neuroinflammation and BMP4-SMAD-related signaling changes in vivo . abstracts.title: Targeting the HPGDS-PGD<sub>2</sub> axis to treat Th17 cell-mediated autoimmunity in multiple sclerosis.
abstracts.abstract: Th17 cells are central drivers of autoimmune pathology, including multiple sclerosis (MS), yet the endogenous metabolic signals that shape their pathogenic differentiation remain incompletely defined. Prostaglandin D₂ (PGD 2 ) is traditionally viewed as an extracellular mediator in allergic diseases. Here, we identify PGD 2 as a cell-intrinsic antagonist of the nuclear receptor PPARγ, thereby promoting Th17 cell differentiation and exacerbating EAE pathology. PGD 2 is selectively elevated in patients with MS compared with healthy individuals. Within the MS cohort, PGD 2 correlates with Th17 cell frequency and disease severity. Consistent with this association, administration of PGD 2 increases the severity of experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) in mice. CD4 + T cell-specific deletion of Hpgds, the key synthase for PGD 2 , impairs Th17 cell polarization and protects against EAE, whereas exogenous PGD 2 restores both Th17 cell responses and disease susceptibility. Importantly, pharmacological inhibition of HPGDS alleviates EAE symptoms in mice. Consistently, HPGDS inhibition suppresses Th17 cell differentiation in both murine and human CD4 + T cells, highlighting its tra…

abstracts.title: Targeting P2Y<sub>12</sub> limits T<sub>H</sub>17 accumulation in the CNS and reduces EAE progression.
abstracts.abstract: Platelets are increasingly recognized as active amplifiers of neuroinflammation in multiple sclerosis and experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE). P2Y12 is an essential ADP receptor that regulates platelet activation and is upregulated in neuroinflammatory lesions. However, its contribution across different effector populations and therapeutic potential in autoimmune diseases of the central nervous system (CNS) remain incompletely defined. Therefore, we characterized P2ry12 expression across different immune and CNS-resident effector populations involved in EAE. To define P2Y12-dependent mechanisms in autoimmune neuroinflammation, we targeted the P2Y12 receptor both genetically and pharmacologically in MOG35-55-induced EAE and monitored disease course and immunopathology. The neuroinflammatory response was profiled by flow cytometry, histology, and cytokine analyses. Pharmacological inhibition with elinogrel or clopidogrel was evaluated in prophylactic and therapeutic treatment regimens. Additionally, prophylactic elinogrel treatment was combined with antibody-mediated platelet depletion during the effector phase of EAE to define the contribution of platelets to the observ…

abstracts.title: Mucin degradation by Akkermansia muciniphila promotes Alistipes-dependent tryptophan metabolism and Th17-driven autoimmunity.
abstracts.abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an autoimmune disorder of the central nervous system associated with alterations in gut commensals, including Akkermansia muciniphila (A. muciniphila). However, its role in MS remains unclear. Here, we report elevated serum lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and anti-LPS IgG levels in patients with relapsing-remitting MS (RRMS), indicating compromised gut barrier integrity. Notably, RRMS patients also exhibited increased serum anti-A. muciniphila IgA and enhanced A. muciniphila-induced Th17 responses in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs). Using experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE), a mouse model of MS, we found that A. muciniphila colonization worsened EAE severity, with increased infiltration of GM-CSF + CD4 + and IL-17A + CD4 + T cells in spinal cord. Mechanistically, A. muciniphila colonization enhanced tryptophan metabolism and elevated levels of aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) agonists, including indole derivatives, during EAE. Although A. muciniphila does not directly metabolize tryptophan, it promotes expansion of tryptophan-utilizing bacterium Alistipes onderdonkii (A. onderdonkii) through mucin degradation. data.warnings_and_cautions: 5 WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS Infections : Serious infections have occurred. Exercise caution when considering the use of COSENTYX in patients with a chronic infection or a history of recurrent infection. If a serious infection develops, discontinue COSENTYX until the infection resolves. ( 5.1 ) Hypersensitivity Reactions : If an anaphylactic reaction or other serious allergic reaction occurs, discontinue COSENTYX immediately and initiate appropriate therapy. ( 5.2 ) Tuberculosis (TB) : Prior to initiating treatment with COSENTYX, evaluate for TB. ( 5.3 ) Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD) : Cases of IBD were observed in clinical trials. Exercise caution when prescribing COSENTYX to patients with IBD. ( 5.4 ) Eczematous Eruptions : Cases of severe eczematous eruptions have occurred in patients receiving COSENTYX. ( 5.5 ) Immunizations : Avoid use of live vaccines in patients treated with COSENTYX. ( 5.7 ) 5.1 Infections COSENTYX may increase the risk of infections. In clinical trials, a higher rate of infections was observed in COSENTYX treated subjects compared to placebo-treated subjects. In placebo-controlled clinical trials in subjects with moderate to severe PsO, higher rates of common infections, such as nasopharyngitis (11.4% versus 8.6%), upper respiratory tract infection (2.5% versus 0.7%) and mucocutaneous infections with candida (1.2% versus 0.3%) were observed in subjects treated with COSENTYX compared to placebo-treated subjects. input.notes: Target IL-17A has been tested in MS in three Phase 2 trials, all by Novartis, using secukinumab (AIN457). One trial was terminated early due to strategic shift, not safety. Secukinumab and ixekizumab are approved for other autoimmune diseases but not MS. Literature from 2026 shows IL-17A's role in MS is debated; some studies suggest it is dispensable in certain models. No stop-risk data from site_risk. Memo will focus on limited trial activity, strategic termination, and mixed mechanistic evidence.

I'll analyze each sentence against its cited sources. Let me go through them one by one.

**Sentence s1**: Claims "Three Phase 2 trials of IL-17A inhibition in multiple sclerosis have been conducted, all by Novartis using secukinumab (AIN457)." Cited source NCT01874340 shows "trials_total":3, "counts_by_phase":{"Phase 2":3}, "companies":{"Novartis":3}, and mentions secukinumab. **Supported**.

**Sentence s2**: Claims early termination due to "strategic development priorities, not safety concerns" and shifting to "another anti-IL-17 antibody deemed to have better potential for MS." Source shows "why_stopped":"Study terminated early based upon development of another anti-IL17 fully human monoclonal antibody with better potential for treating MS patients" and doesn't mention safety concerns. **Supported**.

**Sentence s3**: Claims secukinumab has reached Phase 4 for psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis, and ankylosing spondylitis, but not for multiple sclerosis. Source shows max_phase:4.0 and indications with Phase 4 for those conditions, and no mention of MS. **Supported**.

**Sentence s4**: Claims ixekizumab has reached Phase 4 for psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis but hasn't advanced in multiple sclerosis. Source shows max_phase:4.0 and indications with Phase 4 for psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis, but no MS mentioned. **Supported**.

**Sentence s5**: Claims FDA label includes no MS indication and notes increased infection risk, candidiasis, and IBD caution. Source shows indications list doesn't include MS, mentions infections/IBD warnings, and specifically notes "mucocutaneous infections with candida." **Supported**.

**Sentence s6**: Claims 2026 mouse study found IL-17A dispensable for brain-predominant disease without IFNγ, suggesting not essential for all MS model neuroinflammation. Source abstract states "IL-17A is dispensable for brain-predominant disease in the absence of IFNγ" in HLA-DR3 mice with EAE. **Supported**.

**Sentence s7**: Claims Th17/IL-17A involved in MS pathogenesis but necessity unclear, with disease possible in their absence depending on context. Source abstract mentions Th17/IL-17A involved in MS pathogenesis but doesn't discuss necessity or disease development in their absence - it's more general about Th17 pathways. **Partly supported** - source confirms involvement but doesn't address the necessity claim or disease development in absence.

sections.text: Three Phase 2 trials of IL-17A inhibition in multiple sclerosis have been conducted, all by Novartis using secukinumab (AIN457).

One of the three trials was terminated early due to strategic development priorities, not safety concerns, with Novartis shifting to another anti-IL-17 antibody deemed to have better potential for MS.
Secukinumab has reached Phase 4 for psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis, and ankylosing spondylitis, but not for multiple sclerosis.
Ixekizumab, another IL-17A inhibitor, has also reached Phase 4 for psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis but has not advanced in multiple sclerosis.
The FDA label for secukinumab includes no indication for multiple sclerosis and notes an increased risk of infections and candidiasis, with caution advised for inflammatory bowel disease.

A 2026 study in HLA-DR3 transgenic mice with EAE found that IL-17A is dispensable for brain-predominant disease in the absence of IFNγ, suggesting it may not be essential for all forms of neuroinflammation in MS models.

Recent literature indicates Th17 cells and IL-17A are involved in MS pathogenesis, but their necessity is unclear, with studies showing disease can develop in their absence depending on immune context.

read: Mechanism evidence: IL-17A inhibition has been tested in three Phase 2 trials for MS with no advancement, and recent studies suggest it may not be essential in all neuroinflammatory contexts.
Competitive position: IL-17A inhibitors are approved for other autoimmune conditions but have not progressed in MS; development was deprioritized despite no major safety signals.
Open questions: Is IL-17A necessary for MS pathogenesis given evidence of disease in its absence? Could other Th17-related pathways be more critical?
would_change: New evidence of clinical efficacy in a Phase 2 or Phase 3 trial would change this judgement.
Stronger mechanistic evidence linking IL-17A directly to MS pathology in human-relevant models would support reconsideration.
